subject: Energy
title: Blockchain and Peer-to-Peer Energy
description: A short lesson to help you apply Blockchain and Peer-to-Peer Energy.

hook.text: Blockchain technology could let neighbors trade solar power directly—cutting out the utility middleman.

buildup.text: Your rooftop solar overproduces at noon—a blockchain platform automatically sells the excess to a neighbor.

discovery.text: Brooklyn Microgrid was an early pilot—residents traded locally generated solar energy on a blockchain ledger.

twist.text: Regulators are cautious—peer-to-peer trading challenges existing utility business models and grid management rules.

climax.text: Most projects remain experimental—technical complexity and regulatory barriers have slowed commercial adoption.

punchline.text: Trade solar with your neighbor—blockchain makes it possible.

quiz.question: What could blockchain enable in energy?
